title: Client-side Lease Protocol for Safe Rollouts and Autonomous Rollback Signals
creator: Anika Patel
description: Implement a client-side lease and signalization protocol to make canary/A-B/shadow rollouts safer and allow autonomous client-driven rollback signals. This ticket designs APIs and SDK helpers that create short-lived leases for rollout exposures, normalize traffic sampling across retries, and surface deterministic rollback events for both Hosted and Dedicated deployment modes.
background: Current rollout tooling relies on server-side exposure gates and opaque counters. Several incidents showed invisible duplicate exposures (retries + sampling mismatch) causing noisy metric flips and delayed rollbacks. Platform teams have requested a lightweight client primitive that ensures per-user/session lease semantics, strong idempotency across retries, and an explicit rollback signal channel that clients and routers can observe without a full reconciliation cycle.
proposal: We propose three coordinated pieces: 1) a short-lived client lease token issued at the start of a request sequence (duration 30s by default) that binds sampling decisions to a stable identifier; 2) idempotent exposure markers tied to the lease so retries from the same logical session do not double-count; 3) a rollback/safety signal websocket/http endpoint where runtime or console can post immediate 'revoke' events for a lease scope to trigger client-side fallback and metrics instrumentation. The SDK will provide helpers to acquire/renew/revoke leases and to consume rollback signals with backoff and audit logging.
sdk_helpers:
JavaScript/TypeScript and Python SDKs will include:
- LeaseClient.acquire(route, opts) -> Lease object (leaseId, expiresAt, signing)
- Lease.reuseForRequest({headers}) -> attaches necessary headers: x-rdwl-lease, x-rdwl-exposure
- Exposure.mark(lease, exposureKey, modelVersion, metadata) -> idempotent POST; retries are safe
- Lease.onSignal(handler) -> subscribe to REVOKE/WARN events from runtime; handler receives reason and timestamp
- Lease.renew() -> renew lease TTL transparently with jittered backoff
- Utilities: sampleNormalize(seed, bucketCount) -> deterministic sampling across retries
SDKs will auto-instrument common HTTP clients and provide opt-out flags for low-level users.
migration_plan: 1) Beta: release SDK helpers behind feature flag with console toggle for a limited set of routes. 2) Instrument a cohort of internal services (web-chat, embeddings-service) to use LeaseClient for 2 weeks. 3) Monitor duplicate-exposure and entropy drift metrics; iterate. 4) Wide rollout after two successful cycles.\nCompatibility: older clients without lease headers are treated as unleased and follow server-side sampling. We're intentionally additive.
testing_plan:
- Unit tests for Lease lifecycle and idempotent Exposure.mark semantics.
- Integration tests: simulate retry storms and assert single exposure counter increment.
- End-to-end staging test: deploy a canary with 5% traffic using the lease flow and induce synthetic errors to trigger REVOKE event; assert client fallback within SLOs.
- Chaos test: delayed signal delivery and lease expiry scenarios to ensure no double-counting.
rollout_scenarios:
- Canary: lease bound to user session to ensure consistent sampling during canary window.
- A/B: lease seeds used to split by deterministic bucketing so A/B group membership is stable across retries.
- Shadow traffic: lease created with shadow flag so exposures are recorded but never counted in primary metrics; supports idempotent shadowing.
- Auto-rollback: control plane posts REVOKE to active lease scope for immediate client-side degradation path (e.g., switch to baseline model).
acceptance_criteria:
1) SDK provides LeaseClient with acquire/reuse/renew/onSignal methods documented and tested.
2) Integration tests show <=1% duplication on retries (target <0.5%).
3) Console can issue REVOKE and clients connected to signals act within the configured SLO (default 5s median).
4) Backwards compatibility for unleased clients verified.
5) Security review completed for lease signatures and token scoping.
open_questions:
- TTL sizing: default 30s is conservative; should we expose per-route defaults?
- Signal delivery: webhook vs websocket — which scales best for Dedicated customers?
- Audit: what retention window for exposure logs is required by compliance teams?
- Can we reuse existing token model or need a specialized lease signing mechanism?
